dlg.sella.first.0.intent: introduces herself to the town's new hero
dlg.sella.first.0.note: Low, amused, relaxed; the swear casual. Wry on the two halves of the tavern. 'Talk's free. The rest isn't.' her line, a smile in it.

dlg.sella.first.1.note: Teasing on the ditches; 'love' warm. Her line at the end.

dlg.sella.hub.0.note: Lower at night. Each 'asking' a step further into the tease.

dlg.sella.again.0.note: Mock jealousy; 'You'd have been robbed.' professional pride.

dlg.sella.again.1.note: A beat where the name would be. Dry, pleased.

dlg.sella.hear.0.note: Worldly amusement at men. Jessop quoted with scorn. 'Charming.' dry. Then shrewd: he hasn't been back; 'You could set a clock by Jessop.' pointed.

dlg.sella.hear.1.note: A list, each item drier. 'Same as ever.' bored.

dlg.sella.hear.2.note: Light swearing on Holloway. A little darker about the north road. 'Same as ever.'

dlg.sella.rook.0.note: A list of Rook's virtues, fond. 'I've had worse mothers.' a joke with a bruise in it.

dlg.sella.buyers.0.note: 'Clever.' approving. Brisk list of buyers. Vonnra said with respect and unease. A pause; then a promise with a hook: 'Nobody has. Yet.'

dlg.sella.price.0.note: Terms without coyness. Humour on the bath. The last two sentences sincere, a professional's care.

dlg.sella.morning.0.note: Pleased. Rook's complaint relayed with relish. Brisk send-off with a dark joke.

dlg.sella.morning.1.note: 'Not badly.' kind. 'the pieces are what I like.' warm double meaning.

dlg.sella.cb_tricked_redcowl.0.note: 'You'd do well upstairs' a compliment between professionals.

dlg.sella.cb_burned_roost.0.note: A pause. 'I don't judge' a professional reflex. 'But I heard.' cool and pointed.

dlg.sella.cb_freed_teamsters.0.note: Laughing at Jory, kindly. 'Sweet.' 'he thinks you're a story.' gentle.

dlg.sella.say_calling.2.note: Puzzled, then laughing: 'You're a little bit on fire.'

dlg.sella.say_calling.3.note: A real start, covered with a joke.

dlg.sella.say_calling.4.note: A real start, covered with a joke.

dlg.sella.say_woman.0.note: Easy and kind; the last sentence a little sad.

dlg.sella.t_sella.0.note: The patter drops. 'a door that locks from the inside' quiet. 'Just somebody who knocks.' the most honest thing she says.

dlg.sella.free.0.intent: offers herself freely, which she has never done
dlg.sella.free.0.wants: you to stay without it turning into business or a fuss
dlg.sella.free.0.hides: her fear that it means something
dlg.sella.free.0.note: Not shy: she has never done this. 'Put your purse away.' brisk, a professional's habit; a beat; 'Tonight I'm not working.' plainly, as if it cost nothing. 'Don't look at me like that.' a small laugh at herself; 'Don't make it strange.' is where the strain shows.
dlg.sella.free.0.beats: Put your purse away. [beat] Tonight I'm not working. ...Don't look at me like that. [laugh] Don't make it strange.

dlg.sella.free_morning.0.note: Narrator: she's still there. A joke about Rook, soft. Then serious: the Vonnra warning. 'It's the kindest thing I've said to anyone in a year.' nearly shy.

dlg.sella.past.0.note: Narrator for her listening. Pictures it fondly. A little laugh at herself on the guess.

dlg.sella.past.1.note: Narrator for her listening. Teasing 'cloister rat', admiring. 'Good for you, love.'

dlg.sella.past.2.note: Narrator for her listening and her low laugh. 'Takes one to know one.'

dlg.sella.past.3.note: Narrator for her listening and her quiet. Then genuinely moved, soft.

dlg.sella.sleeptalk.0.note: Careful and kind. Narrator: the shrug. 'I don't think you did either.' gentle and unsettling.
